dataset: NASA Orion / Artemis Crewed Lunar & Launch Vehicle Reference Data
archivedDataNotice: Sourced public engineering figures from NASA Orion, ESA European Service Module (ESM), NASA Space Launch System (SLS), SpaceX Falcon Heavy / Falcon 9, and ULA Vulcan Centaur reference sheets. Additive part masses are split to avoid double-counting solar wings and consumables already bundled in Orion/ESM gross weights; FlightSim stage parameters preserve real Isp/engine ratios scaled to the procedural 3D rocket stack.

parts.name: Orion-Class Crew Module (CM)
parts.notes: Orion CM dry/crew baseline (~9,300 kg dry; ~10,387 kg liftoff with internal consumables & cargo), Avcoat heat shield, 4 crew capacity.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Orion Spacecraft Overview & Fact Sheet

parts.name: Service Module — Flyby Propellant Load
parts.notes: ~5,980 kg bare ESM structure/AJ10-190 + 3,500 kg hypergolic propellant: enough for free-return flyby on Medium launcher, insufficient for lunar orbit insertion.
parts.sourceLabel: ESA / NASA European Service Module (ESM) Reference

parts.name: European Service Module (ESM) — Full Lunar Load
parts.notes: ~5,580 kg bare ESM bus/AJ10-190/tanks + 9,000 kg MON/MMH propellant (excluding 480 kg solar wings counted separately; full Orion CM+ESM TLI stack ~26,520 kg).
parts.sourceLabel: ESA / NASA Orion ESM Technical Specifications

parts.name: ECLSS Consumables (7-Day Nominal)
parts.notes: O2, N2, potable water, and amine CO2 scrubbers for 4 crew (~1 week; 9 days w/ CM reserve).

parts.name: ECLSS Consumables (14-Day Extended Margin)
parts.notes: Extended O2, water, and CO2 scrubbing consumables supporting 14–21 day Artemis profiles.

parts.name: ESM 4-Wing X-Configuration Solar Arrays
parts.notes: Four 7-meter deployable solar wings generating ~11.2 kW at 1 AU.
parts.sourceLabel: ESA / Airbus Orion ESM Solar Array Specs

parts.name: Crew Radiation Storm Shelter & HERA Dosimetry
parts.notes: Hydrogen-rich radiation shelter stowage kit + NASA HERA particle dosimeters for DONKI solar energetic particle (SEP) events.

rockets.name: Light (Single-Core Medium-Heavy Class)
rockets.payloadToMoonNote: Game-balanced single-core TLI limit (~9 t; real Falcon 9 expendable is ~4–5.5 t TLI / ~8.3 t GTO and Vulcan VC0/VC2 spans ~4.8–9.5 t TLI). Cannot lift a full crewed Orion stack.
rockets.notes: Single-stick kerolox/methalox reference for FlightSim; too small for crewed Orion to the Moon.
rockets.sourceLabel: SpaceX Falcon 9 / ULA Vulcan Centaur Reference

rockets.name: Medium (3-Core Heavy Class)
rockets.payloadToMoonNote: NASA LSP cites 15,310 kg at C3 = -1 km2/s2 for Falcon Heavy Expendable; game-balanced to 20,000 kg so players can fly the light flyby stack (19,940 kg) while full lunar orbit stack (25,040–26,490 kg) requires Heavy (SLS Block 1).

falconHeavy.upperStage: 1x Merlin 1D Vacuum (981 kN, 348 s vac, ~107.5 t prop)

rockets.notes: Triple-core booster layout matching Rocket.tsx Medium stack (2 side boosters + center core).
rockets.sourceLabel: SpaceX Falcon Heavy & NASA LSP Performance Portal

rockets.name: Heavy (NASA SLS Block 1)
rockets.payloadToMoonNote: NASA SLS Block 1 official capability: >27 metric tons (27,000+ kg) to TLI.

slsBlock1.boosters: 2x 5-Segment PBAN SRBs (~16 MN each, ~631,495 kg prop each, ~268 s vac)
slsBlock1.coreStageEngines: 4x RS-25 at 109% RPL (1,860 kN SL / 2,279 kN vac each; 366 s SL / 452.3 s vac)

rockets.notes: Exact NASA SLS Block 1 SRB, RS-25 Core Stage, and ICPS RL10B-2 parameters. Note: FlightSim currently scales stage masses down for fast ascent, so tune FlightSim TLI cutoff if substituting full 2.5M kg real SLS liftoff mass.
rockets.sourceLabel: NASA Space Launch System (SLS) & Core Stage Fact Sheets
